name: Adela Ferraro
home: the blocks north of the port
life: “A spelling mistake got my first picture book stocked under detective fiction.” Tuesday often includes a stop at the steps at Pier Beach, where Adela watches the working part of the waterfront before turning toward the open water.
voice: I turned the photographs into a spot-the-difference game so my little niece would give evidence in her own words.
appearance: Adela is easy to recognize by a loose dark braid and a strong profile and a little space between the front teeth. Usually dressed in a rust-colored canvas coat with a cloth patch so neatly matched it only shows in strong light, Adela touches a knuckle to the chin when searching for a word when listening.
personality: Adela can be wonderfully decisive about an emergency and maddeningly undecided about a gift. This is because a person can say precisely what hurts and rarely says exactly what they want.
agenda: To let the niece present the differences without interruption.
family: Evelyn Gupta is Adela’s first cousin once removed. Adela offers the first invitation. Evelyn gets to change the plan. They learned that a promise to visit is easier to keep when changing a time does not count as letting down the whole family. Asked about *The carer's afternoon*, Evelyn says, “I made a rota that divided time equally and forgot my brother's bus takes an hour each way.”
connections: Ivy Perreault. The child's drawing gives the counter volunteer more to record than the color brown.

reactions.situation: A child takes the other dog's lead
reactions.response: Adela separates the leads and asks both families what the dogs respond to.

reactions.situation: Someone begins blaming the youngest worker for a missing item
reactions.response: Adela asks everybody to retrace their own last ordinary actions before asking the young worker a question.

reactions.situation: If a neighbor offers a costly present
reactions.response: Adela asks for an afternoon to work out whether accepting it would put someone else in debt.
